nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The Zn-NiMoO₄ SNWs were synthesized using a typical solvothermal method, employing Na₂MoO₄, Ni(NO₃)₂, and Zn(NO₃)₂ as the metal precursors, and oleylamine and oleic acid as surfactants (details provided in the Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: The Zn-NiMoO₄ SNWs were synthesized using a typical solvothermal method... (details provided in the Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction
nodes.procedure: Zn-NiMoO₄ SNWs precatalyst underwent surface reconstruction during OER testing in 1 M KOH electrolyte via multiple LSV cycles until stability reached by third cycle. Mo completely leached out (97+% mass loss), Ni oxidized to Ni³⁺ᵟ state (avg +3.22), Zn to higher oxidation state (avg +3.67), forming γ-Zn-NiOOH SNWs while maintaining subnanowire morphology.
nodes.source_text: Figure 2a illustrates the OER activity gradually increased with the increase in LSV cycles and reached stability by the third LSV, indicating that a rapid surface reconstruction process occurred during the OER process... The NiMoO₄ and Zn-NiMoO₄ SNWs catalysts after the surface reconstruction were denoted as NiOOH and Zn-NiOOH SNWs.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images reveal ultrafine nanowires with diameter of approximately 1 nm and length of tens of micrometers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images revealed that the morphology of the obtained Zn-NiMoO4 consists of neatly aligned ultrafine nanowires with a diameter of approximately 1 nm and a length of tens of micrometers (Figures 1a,b and S1).

properties.description: Aligned, interwoven nanofibers with diameters comparable to 50 nm scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms nanowire morphology with diameter of 1.1 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) results in Figure 1c further confirm that the morphology of Zn-NiMoO4 consists of nanowires with a diameter of 1.1 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAXRD shows distinct peak at 2.27° indicative of periodic arrangement between SNWs with spacing of 3.9 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The small-angle X-ray diffraction analysis (SAXRD, Figures 1d and S3a) revealed a distinct peak at 2.27°, indicative of a periodic arrangement between the SNWs with a spacing of 3.9 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 27.3°, 29.8°, 31.8°, and 53.5° corresponding to (112), (220), (222), and (150) planes of NiMoO4·nH2O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the product (Figure 1e) reveals four dominant peaks situated at 27.3, 29.8, 31.8, and 53.5°, corresponding to the (112), (220), (222), and (150) planes of nickel molybdate hydrate (NiMoO4·nH2O, JCPDS file no. 13-0128).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM confirms parallel-aligned subnanowire morphology with low crystallinity; d-spacings of 2.81 Å and 3.26 Å indexed to (222) and (112) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed d spacing of 2.81 and 3.26Å could be indexed to the (222) and (112) crystal planes of NiMoO4.

properties.description: Granular nanostructure visible in TEM with lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS elemental mapping show uniform distribution of Zn, Ni, Mo, and O throughout Zn-NiMoO4 SNWs without segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image and EDS elemental mapping demonstrated the uniform distribution of Zn, Ni, Mo, and O throughout the entire Zn-NiMoO4 SNWs without composition segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Zn 2p peaks at 1021.3 and 1044.4 eV (Zn2+), Ni 2p peaks shift ~0.22 eV to higher binding energy after Zn incorporation, Mo 6+ peak negative shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Zn 2p spectra (Figure S6a), distinct peaks were observed at 1021.3 and 1044.4 eV... In the Ni 2p spectrum (Figure S6c), the doublet peaks at 855.6 and 873.2 eV attributed to Ni2+ in NiMoO4 shifting (~0.22 eV) toward higher binding energy after Zn incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms elemental composition Zn:Ni/Mo = 0.07:1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental composition of Zn-NiMoO4 was further confirmed by inductively coupled plasma analysis spectrometry (ICP, Table S1) to be Zn:Ni/Mo = 0.07:1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XRD shows disappearance of NiMoO4 peaks and emergence of γ-NiOOH peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the initial Zn-NiMoO4, notable changes are observed in the XRD spectrum (Figure S15), characterized by the disappearance of NiMoO4 diffraction peaks and the emergence of diffraction peaks attributed to γ-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS: Mo6+ signal disappears, Ni2+ shifts to higher energy with Ni3+δ peaks at 856.6 and 871.4 eV, Zn2+ shows positive shift indicating Zn2+δ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the signal of Mo6+ in Zn-NiMoO4 disappears after OER... For Ni 2p, the binding energy of Ni2+ shifted to higher energies, accompanied by the appearance of peaks at 856.6 and 871.4 eV corresponding to Ni3+δ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows elevated absorption edge vs Ni2O3 indicating Ni3+δ oxidation state (average +3.22).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f shows that the Ni K-edge absorption edge positions of the Zn-NiOOH SNWs were elevated in energy relative to the Ni2O3 reference samples, indicating an increase in the oxidation state of Ni to Ni3+δ in the reconstructed catalyst... The average oxidation state of Ni in Zn-NiOOH, determined from the half-peak K-edge energy, is approximately +3.22.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ni-O at 1.44 Å and Ni-Ni at 2.38 Å of γ-NiOOH; shortened Ni-O bond length vs reported NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding Ni K-edge Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structures (FT-EXAFS) spectra display two distinct peaks at 1.44 and 2.38Å (no phase correction, Figure 2g), corresponding to the Ni-O and Ni-Ni bonds of γ-NiOOH reported in the literature... Notably, the Ni-O bond length in Zn-NiOOH is shortened compared to reported NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows γ-NiOOH peaks at 476 and 557 cm⁻¹ emerging at 1.3 V vs RHE for Zn-NiMoO4 (vs 1.5 V for NiMoO4); O-O⁻ at 1079 cm⁻¹ at 1.4 V confirms LOM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Particularly noteworthy is the emergence of the γ-NiOOH Raman peaks in Zn-NiMoO4 SNWs at 1.3 V vs RHE... the Raman signals at around 1079 cm⁻¹ assigned to the stretching vibration of O-O⁻ species were observed for Zn-NiOOH SNWs.

nodes.characterization_summary: 18O-labeled DEMS shows m/z 32,34,36 signals with increasing 34/32 and 36/32 ratios exceeding natural 18O abundance, confirming LOM for Zn-NiOOH vs AEM for NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Zn-NiOOH SNWs differentially revealed signals at m/z = 32, m/z = 34, and m/z = 36... the 34O2 to 32O2 and 36O2 to 32O2 ratios gradually increase with the applied voltage, exceeding the natural abundance of 18O in water.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability TEM/STEM shows unchanged subnanowire morphology; EDS confirms uniform Zn, Ni, O distribution with nearly absent Mo signal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the subnanowire morphology of the Zn-NiMoO4 SNWs catalyst after the stability test remains unchanged, and EDS mapping indicates that Zn, Ni, and O are still uniformly distributed on the nanowires, while the signal of Mo is nearly completely absent.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability ICP shows Zn/Ni ratio 0.06:1, Mo undetectable; mass loss Zn 0.8%, Ni 1.7%, Mo >97%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further ICP-OES analysis confirmed that, after the stability test, the Zn/Ni ratio in the Zn-NiOOH SNWs was 0.06:1 (Table S7), while Mo was undetectable... the mass loss values of Zn and Ni in Zn-NiMoO4 SNWs after the 800-h stability test are as low as 0.8 and 1.7%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows improved conductivity after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements were conducted before and after activation. The results revealed improvements in both the conductivity...

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl measurements show increased electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results revealed improvements in both the conductivity and electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) of the activated Zn-NiOOH SNWs catalyst (Figures S7 and S8 and Table S2)

nodes.characterization_summary: Zn K-edge XANES shows positive absorption edge shift relative to ZnO indicating higher oxidation state (+3.67 average).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similar to the phenomenon observed in Ni K-edge, the Zn K-edge XANES of Zn-NiOOH demonstrates a positive absorption edge shift relative to ZnO reference samples (Figure 2h), suggesting the Zn-NiOOH has a higher oxidation state than ZnO. The average oxidation state of Zn is confirmed to be +3.67.

nodes.characterization_summary: Zn K-edge FT-EXAFS shows prominent Zn-O peak at 1.53 Å; absence of Zn-Zn bonds indicates isolated atomic dispersion of Zn in NiOOH lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Zn K-edge FT-EXAFS spectrum of Zn-NiOOH revealed a prominent peak at around 1.53Å (no phase correction, Figure 2i), indicative of Zn-O coordination. It is noteworthy that the absence of significant Zn-Zn bonds observed suggests the isolated atomic dispersion of Zn within the lattice of NiOOH.
